content.value_statement: Modern .NET work requires clean architecture, async safety, testing, and performance awareness. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused C# design, refactoring, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Guides modern C# syntax, including records, pattern matching, and nullable reference types.
Supports ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework, Blazor, and broader .NET ecosystem decisions.
Recommends SOLID design, composition, enterprise patterns, and microservice architecture when relevant.
Helps improve async and concurrent code using async/await and Task Parallel Library patterns.
Suggests unit testing approaches with xUnit, NUnit, Moq, and FluentAssertions.
Can outline BenchmarkDotNet checks, analyzers, EditorConfig, and NuGet package guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated text, not a compiled or tested .NET project by itself.
It does not replace runtime profiling, production telemetry, or manual code review.
It needs project context to choose correct framework, package, and architecture options.
It does not include executable helper scripts or automated migration tools.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Services
use_cases.description: Modernize C# services with nullable references, records, clearer error handling, and safer async patterns.

use_cases.title: Design Enterprise APIs
use_cases.description: Plan ASP.NET Core architecture, dependency boundaries, data access patterns, and test strategy for maintainable services.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Create focused unit test plans using common .NET testing libraries and meaningful mock boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review C# Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small class or method.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C# code for readability, nullable safety, async issues, and simple test opportunities. Explain each recommendation briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this component using modern C# features where useful. Preserve behavior, call out risks, and suggest focused unit tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for ASP.NET Core or enterprise code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET service for this requirement. Include boundaries, data access, validation, error handling, async flow, and test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and Validate
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this .NET performance concern. Propose measurement steps, likely bottlenecks, safer optimizations, and BenchmarkDotNet validation points.

output_examples.input: Review an async repository method that blocks on a task result.
output_examples.output: The response explains the deadlock risk, recommends await throughout the call chain, and lists unit tests for success and failure paths.

output_examples.input: Plan an ASP.NET Core service for customer order processing.
output_examples.output: The response outlines controllers, validation, application services, persistence boundaries, observability, error handling, and a focused test plan.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow allocation-heavy parsing routine.
output_examples.output: The response recommends profiling first, then evaluates spans, value types, pooling risks, and benchmark cases before changing behavior.

best_practices: Provide the target .NET version, framework, and project constraints before asking for architecture guidance.
Ask for tests and validation steps with every refactor or performance change.
Share relevant code boundaries so recommendations match real dependencies and ownership.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad rewrites without behavior requirements or regression test expectations.
Do not optimize code before measuring the bottleneck with reliable profiling or benchmarks.
Do not mix database access, validation, business rules, and transport logic in one review request.

faq.question: What C# versions does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on modern C# features, including records, pattern matching, nullable reference types, and async patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate unit tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest tests using xUnit, NUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions, and similar .NET testing tools.

faq.question: Does it run or compile code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and generated content. You still need local builds, tests, and reviews.

faq.question: Can it help with ASP.NET Core architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan service boundaries, dependency flow, validation, persistence, error handling, and test strategy.

faq.question: Is it useful for performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest profiling steps, BenchmarkDotNet scenarios, memory improvements, and safer optimization options.

faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
